purpose: Training data for the Urgency classifier. Every source here is published, citable and openly downloadable without credentials. The credentialed primary dataset named by the spec is not in this repository.

sources.title: Evaluation of prognostic patient treatment models with emphasis on the three levels of triage for an emergency severity index in the Emergency Department
sources.citation: Hoseini, Benyamin. (2022). Evaluation of prognostic patient treatment models with emphasis on the three levels of triage for an emergency severity index in the Emergency Department [Data set]. Harvard Dataverse, V1.1. https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/7SOYC7
sources.label_note: The source records a three-level ED triage category in which level 1 is the most urgent, confirmed by inspection: level 1 has the lowest Glasgow Coma Scale, the highest ventilation rate and the highest in-hospital mortality. The mapping is one-to-one onto the three Urgency Levels.

fields_derived.oxygen_saturation_percent: spo2_fio2 * Fio2 / 100, because the source publishes the SpO2/FiO2 ratio and the inspired oxygen fraction rather than saturation directly

sources.note: One row per ED admission over a year at a single centre. No free text, so this source contributes no Symptom Groups. It is the only open source found whose three-level label is balanced enough to train and cross-validate a three-class model.

considered_but_not_used.title: MIMIC-IV-ED Demo 2.2 (PhysioNet, ODC-ODbL, https://doi.org/10.13026/jzz5-vs76)
considered_but_not_used.reason: Openly downloadable and the only open source found that records pain, a presenting complaint and ESI acuity together, so it was the preferred candidate. Its open subset is 100 patients (222 triage rows), and only 2 of those rows are ESI 4-5. A three-class model cannot be cross-validated on two examples of one class, and combining it with this source put the two label scales and two different missingness regimes into one intercept, which made the predictions collapse to High. It is recorded here so the search is auditable and the decision can be revisited.

considered_but_not_used.title: MIMIC-IV-ED full database (PhysioNet, credentialed)
considered_but_not_used.reason: The dataset the spec names as primary. It requires credentialed access and a data use agreement; it is not available on this machine, so it could not be used for this artefact.

limitations: The published source records no pain level, no illness duration and no presenting complaint. Those dimensions are present in the feature vector but constant in training, so the shipped artefact gives them a zero coefficient.

This is an interim development model trained on an open dataset, not the primary-dataset model the spec describes. Cross-validated accuracy is at the level of the majority-class baseline, which ticket 15 measures on the rubric-labelled corpus, not here.
The source is a single centre's three-level triage category, harmonised one-to-one onto the three Urgency Levels. That mapping is a documented assumption, not a validated harmonisation.
The free-text complaint is never a feature: only Symptom Groups recognised from it would be, and this source supplies none.
